title: Radiologic Features of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis
brief_summary: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is an opportunistic infection that primarily affects recipients of solid organ transplants (SOTs) and patients with chemotherapy- induced neutropenia.Although both of these populations are at high risk for IPA, they differ with regards to the specific defects in host defense mechanisms that increase their risk for IPA. Chemotherapy- induced neutropenia is the principal defect affecting patients with hematologic malignancies, whereas transplant recipients tend to have dysfunctional T cells and phagocytes, as a result of immunosuppressive drug therapy. Thus, the patterns of IPA-related infection and inflammation may differ according to the type of underlying immune defect. Although the clinical and radiological features of IPA in patients with neutropenia have been extensively studied, little is known about the characteristics of IPA in SOT recipients. The investigators therefore compared the IPA- related clinical and radiological findings in SOT recipients with those of neutropenic patients.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* IPA cases with solid organ transplant recipients and hematologic disease patients
* proven and probable invasive pulmonary aspergillosis by modified EORTC/MSG criteria

Exclusion Criteria:

* under 16 years old
* possible cases of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
study_population: All adult patients who are diagnosed with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA)between January 2008 and February 2010.
